title: Ordinary homotopy Hom as quotient algebraic Hom cohomology
statement: Let X,A,J,U be as in def-sfb-adic-perfect-reduction-model-complexes with the same surjectivity of final evaluation for epimorphisms of set sheaves. Let P,Q be bounded integer cochain complexes of finite-projective A-modules. Let C_n(P), C_n(Q), alpha_n(P), alpha_n(Q) and tau_n be the actual ordinary models and scalar-balancing maps of that definition. Let F_n be sections at the slice terminal object of the constant A-module sheaf on H^0(moduleHomComplex(P,Q)/J^(n+1)), with canonical quotient cohomology transitions. There are bijections e_n from Hom in the homotopy category between C_n(P) and C_n(Q) to F_n. For every chain map f:C_(n+1)(P)->C_(n+1)(Q), e_n of the homotopy class of alpha_n(P)^(-1), then ordinary change(tau_n)(f), then alpha_n(Q), equals the quotient transition applied to e_(n+1) of the homotopy class of f. No derived localization, derived Hom, or choice of derived comparison is part of this assertion.

proof.text: Apply the all-degree quotient Hom evaluation comparison. Its successor equation, extended to additive chain maps by the signed Hom differential, gives a commuting square of ordinary abelian-group complexes. The actual scalarHomMap is constructed from Cochain.map, precomposition by the source balancing inverse and postcomposition by the target balancing.

Sections of constant module sheaves preserve finite limits and finite colimits on any small site, by the existing constant-module section properties proof (its exactness part does not require Noetherianity). Compose with the forgetful functor to abelian groups. The canonical exact-functor homology comparison identifies H^0 of each realized quotient Hom complex with sections of algebraic quotient H^0.

Mathlib homologyAddEquiv and CohomologyClass.homAddEquiv identify H^0 of the ordinary global Hom complex with Hom in the homotopy category; remove the zero shift using shiftFunctorZero. On a chain map the inverse equivalence is its cocycle class. Prove this class formula and its naturality under scalarHomMap by cycles inclusion injectivity and naturality of the homology projection. Apply homology to the chain square and use mapHomologyIso_hom_naturality for the quotient transition. This gives the required successor identity on every actual chain map.

theorem adicPerfectModelHomCohomology (X : Scheme.{u})
    {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] (J : Ideal A)
    (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X)
    (_hU : AdicResidueSliceWeaklyContractible.{u, v} X U)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{max v (u + 1)} A) ℤ)
    (a b c d : ℤ) (_ha : P.IsStrictlyGE a) (_hb : P.IsStrictlyLE b)
    (_hc : Q.IsStrictlyGE c) (_hd : Q.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (_hP : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (P.X i) ∧ Module.Projective A (P.X i))
    (_hQ : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Finite A (Q.X i) ∧ Module.Projective A (Q.X i)) :
    let F := AdicCohomology.tower J ((CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex P Q).sc 0) ⋙
      AdicCohomology.sections
        ((coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X).over U) (Over.mk (𝟙 U)) ⋙
      CategoryTheory.forget (ModuleCat A)
    let H := fun n : ℕ ↦ HomotopyCategory.quotient
      (Mod ((finite (coefficientProEtaleModelTopology.{u, v} X) A J n).over U)) (.up ℤ)
    ∃ e : ∀ n : ℕ,
        ((H n).obj (adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U P n) ⟶
          (H n).obj (adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U Q n)) ≃ F.obj (op n),
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (f : adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U P (n + 1) ⟶
          adicPerfectQuotientComplex.{u, v} X J U Q (n + 1)),
        e n ((H n).map ((adicPerfectQuotientStep.{u, v} X J U P n).inv ≫
            ((change (adicPerfectQuotientScalarStep.{u, v} X J U n)).mapHomologicalComplex
              (.up ℤ)).map f ≫ (adicPerfectQuotientStep.{u, v} X J U Q n).hom)) =
          F.map (homOfLE (Nat.le_succ n)).op (e (n + 1) ((H (n + 1)).map f))
